text: dsh-n8n-plugin 是面向 DSH Web 的 n8n 工作流运维插件。它把实例设置页、主机端 API 路由和 Agent 工具接入同一实例注册表，用户登记实例别名、地址与 API Key 后，Agent 可按别名操作。主要功能包括浏览和读写工作流、发布与克隆工作流、校验工作流 JSON、查看或取消执行，以及管理标签和调用 webhook。设置页负责配置实例，工具负责日常运维，适合希望在 DSH 对话中管理 n8n 自动化的用户。使用前需要可访问的 n8n 实例及其 API Key，实例信息保存在 DSH 本地目录。

dsh-n8n-plugin brings n8n workflow operations to DSH Web. Register instances in Settings, then use agent tools to manage workflows, validate JSON, review executions, manage tags, and call webhooks. It requires an n8n instance and API key.

能不能在 DSH 里发布、取消发布或复制自动化流程

帮我查询或调整工作流上的标签
I want to manage my n8n workflows from a DSH chat.
Can I inspect execution history and errors without opening the automation UI?
Help me validate a workflow JSON document before I send it to my instance.
I need one place to register several n8n environments and switch between them by alias.
dsh-n8n-plugin 的功能「工作流管理」：Agent 可按实例别名筛选、读取、创建、更新、删除、发布或克隆 n8n 工作流，并查看工作流节点与标签。通过对应的 n8n_workflow_* 工具调用。
dsh-n8n-plugin 的功能「工作流 JSON 校验」：在发送到实例前离线检查文档结构、节点参数、图连线和表达式，并返回错误与提示。通过 n8n_workflow_validate 工具触发。
dsh-n8n-plugin 的功能「执行记录」：按工作流或状态列出执行、读取详情，并可取消执行。通过 n8n_executions、n8n_execution_get 和 n8n_execution_cancel 工具操作。
dsh-n8n-plugin 的功能「实例设置」：在 DSH Web 设置页登记多个 n8n 实例的别名、地址和凭证，并设置默认实例；Agent 工具通过别名选择目标。界面与工具共用实例存储。
dsh-n8n-plugin 使用前须知：需要为目标 n8n 实例提供 API Key；可直接登记，也可引用环境变量或密钥文件，实例配置写入 DSH 本地目录。

dsh-n8n-plugin README · ✨ Why dsh-n8n-plugin：Most n8n integrations have you paste a base URL and an API key into every conversation. This plugin makes n8n a **first-class citizen of DeepSeek Harness**: one settings page, one instance registry, and 21 agent tools that share it.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · One alias away from any environment：Instances are registered once under **Settings → n8n instances** — an alias (`prod`, `staging`, `local`, …), a base URL and an API key. Every tool call picks its target by alias, so the same instruction works against any environment without repeating credentials.
section: One alias away from any environment

text: dsh-n8n-plugin README · One registry, two surfaces, zero drift：The Settings page and the agent tools read **one and the same store** — what you configure in the GUI is exactly what the agent sees. The split of duties is deliberate: agents can **list** instances but can never create or edit one, because an API key must not be dictated through a conversation.
section: One registry, two surfaces, zero drift

text: dsh-n8n-plugin README · Validate offline, publish with confidence：`n8n_workflow_validate` checks the full workflow document in layers before anything is sent: **structure** (unique node ids and names — connections are keyed by name, connection targets that actually exist, webhook nodes paired with their `Respond to Webhook` responder), **per-node parameters** (webhook path/httpMethod/responseMode, scheduleTrigger `rule.interval`, httpRequest `url`, code-node bodies and more), **topology** (a trigger exists and every node is reachable, IF/Switch branch wiring, SplitInBatches loop-back edge, AI Agent language-model link), and **expressions** (balanced `{{ }}`, a warning for missing `= ` prefix) — all without contacting the instance.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · Keys never leave this machine：API keys live only in `~/.dsh/dsh-n8n-plugin.json` with `0600` permissions. Every response masks them to the last four characters, and the Settings page never echoes a full key back.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · Built for n8n's moving API：Publishing uses the modern `POST /workflows/{id}/publish` and falls back to the legacy `activate` only on a 404. Version differences beyond that are one raw `n8n_api` call away.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🧩 Agent tools：| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `n8n_instances` | List instances (alias, URL, masked key, default). Agents cannot create or edit instances |
| `n8n_workflows` | List workflows (filter by active / name / tags; cursor pagination) |
| `n8n_workflow_get` | Read a full workflow document |
| `n8n_workflow_create` | Create from JSON, optionally publishing immediately |
| `n8n_workflow_update` | Replace a workflow document, optionally changing its published state; keeping `versionId` enables the concurrency guard |
| `n8n_workflow_delete` | Delete a workflow (its triggers stop) |
| `n8n_workflow_publish` | Publish (activate) / unpublish (deactivate) |
| `n8n_workflow_validate` | Offline JSON validation in four layers: structure / per-node parameters / topology / expressions, no instance contacted |
| `n8n_workflow_clone` | Clone a workflow: definition + tags, unpublished by default |
| `n8n_workflow_tags` | Read or replace a workflow's tags (by tag ids or names) |
| `n8n_executions` | List executions (filter by workflow id / status) |
| `n8n_execution_get` | Read one execution as a structured view: status, duration, per-node results and error summar

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🧩 Agent tools：The workflow-JSON reference, a field-tested **pitfall list** and **ready-made templates** live in [`knowledge/workflow-guide.md`](knowledge/workflow-guide.md) (templates in [`knowledge/templates/`](knowledge/templates/): webhook lead capture, scheduled sync, error notify, and AI chat — tweak parameters and ship). With `announceToAgent` on, the prompt names that file's absolute path so the agent can read it on demand. Tool descriptions and user-facing messages are written in Chinese; tool names, parameter names and n8n protocol vocabulary (field names, node types, status enums) intentionally stay in English.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🖥️ Instance management：| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Alias | Starts with a letter or digit; letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` only; at most 64 chars. The target identifier for every tool |
| Base URL | `https://n8n.example.com`, `http://localhost:5678`, optionally with a sub-path; a trailing `/api/v1` may be included and is normalized away |
| API key | Create it in n8n under **Settings → n8n API**. When editing, leave blank to keep the stored key |
| Description | Optional note |
| Default | The instance new work defaults to; only one exists, and deleting it promotes the first remaining entry |

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🖥️ Instance management：The **Test** button calls `GET /workflows?limit=1` on the spot and reports latency — or the exact failure: connection refused, DNS, timeout, TLS, 401.

All instance data lives in one file:

```
~/.dsh/dsh-n8n-plugin.json     # $DSH_HOME/dsh-n8n-plugin.json — file 0600 / directory 0700
```

Writes are atomic (temp file + rename); a corrupted file is quarantined as `.corrupt-<timestamp>` instead of taking the plugin down.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · Manual install (without `dsh plugin`)：1. Place the package at `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-n8n-plugin` (`DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh`) — unzip the tarball or copy the directory.
2. Add the plugin row to that profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
   - insert:
       - id: n8n
         name: 'dsh-n8n-plugin'
   ```

3. Restart the app.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · Manual install (without `dsh plugin`)：The bundled `cordis.patch.yml` is the package-level patch used when the package is listed in `dsh.profile.bundles`; inserting the row directly into the profile is the simpler path.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · ⚙️ How it works：A standard double-sided DSH package: a host half (`lib/`) and a browser half (`client/index.js`, no build step).

```
Settings page (browser)                        Agent (model)
  │                                              │
  ├─ GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE ───┐                  ├─ 21 × n8n_* tools
  │  /api/dsh-n8n-plugin/*    │                  │

dsh-n8n-plugin README · ⚙️ How it works：- **Host half** — `lib/index.js` registers routes, the 21 tools and the optional prompt section from one `apply()`; `lib/store.js` owns the registry (atomic writes, `0600`, corrupt-file quarantine); `lib/n8n.js` is the API v1 client (30 s timeout, merged abort signals, `accept-encoding: identity`) plus a direct webhook caller and an execution wait poller; `lib/http.js` enforces the loopback fence; `lib/mount-once.js` guarantees one mount per package and profile.
- **Browser half** — `client/index.js` renders the Settings section and talks to the same routes, so GUI and agent always agree.
- **Prompt guidance** — `lib/guidance.js` emits the system-prompt section; it renders only when n8n_* tools are visible in the session.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · ⚙️ Configuration：Two boolean flags live in the plugin's `config` inside the profile patch. Both are `volatile()`: an edit reaches the running instance **without a restart** — the loader announces the change and the plugin re-registers its surfaces in place.

```yaml
- id: n8n
  name: 'dsh-n8n-plugin'
  config:
    enabled: true          # master switch: routes, tools, prompt section

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🛡️ Security model：- `/api/dsh-n8n-plugin/*` accepts loopback requests only, validating the socket address, `Host`, `Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site`; any request carrying `X-Forwarded-For` / `CF-Connecting-IP` is refused. Never expose this page through a reverse proxy.
- Request bodies are capped at 256 KiB, and responses are sent `no-store`.
- API keys support three registration modes with priority **environment-variable reference (`apiKeyEnv`) > key-file reference (`apiKeyFile`) > inline (`apiKey`)**; a configured reference that cannot be resolved fails the call outright instead of silently falling back. Inline keys are plaintext in a `0600` user-owned file — the same trust model as `~/.n8n` or a `n8n-api.sh` environment file. Responses only carry the last four characters.
- Agents can read the instance list but cannot create or edit an instance: an API key must not be dictated through a conversation.
- Each instance can be switched to **read-only (`readOnly`)**: every state-changing tool call (create/update/delete/publish/clone/tag writes/execution cancel/webhook call/non-GET `n8n_api`) is then refused with a hint on where to turn the flag off.
- Every guarde

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🛠 Development：Requires Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24`.

```sh
npm run check             # syntax check over every source file
```

Layout:

```
lib/index.js             plugin entry (Config, apply, route/tool/prompt registration)
lib/store.js             instance store (atomic write, 0600, corrupt-file quarantine)
lib/n8n.js               n8n public API v1 client (+ direct webhook call, execution wait)
lib/routes.js            /api/dsh-n8n-plugin routes (loopback fence)

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 📦 Publishing：```sh
npm pack                 # writes dsh-n8n-plugin-0.2.0.tgz (lib/, client/, knowledge/, cordis.patch.yml, icon.svg, both READMEs)
npm publish              # publishes to the default registry once you are logged in
```

> The package name appears in three places at once — `package.json`, the cordis row in `cordis.patch.yml`, and the browser module id in `client/index.js`. If you publish under your own scope, update all three together.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🔐 Permissions & compatibility：- **Permissions**: writes one JSON file under the harness home (`~/.dsh` / `$DSH_HOME`); makes outbound HTTP(S) calls to the registered n8n instances; serves a loopback-only route family through the host's web server. **No** command execution, no shell.
- **Compatibility**: DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.2` (declared as both `engines.dsh` and `dsh.engines.dsh`), Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24`, n8n public API v1 (1.x and later; publishing has a modern/legacy fallback).
- **Lifecycle**: no `preinstall` / `install` / `postinstall` scripts — install and use.
- **Dependency posture**: the only runtime dependency is `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`; every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` package and `react` are optional peer dependencies — the plugin never re-installs, replaces or shadows official components.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · 🤖 Model experience：- 21 `n8n_*` tools (table above); `n8n_instances` and `n8n_workflow_validate` are the safe, read-mostly entry points.
- A run loop in one chain: `n8n_workflow_publish` → `n8n_webhook_call` (trigger + wait) → `n8n_execution_get` to re-inspect — deploy, run, verify.
- Housekeeping is one call each: `n8n_workflow_clone` (copy a workflow with its tags, unpublished), `n8n_workflow_tags` (read/replace a workflow's tags), `n8n_tag_create/update/delete`, and `n8n_execution_cancel` for a stuck run.
- An optional system-prompt section (`announceToAgent`) teaches the alias convention and points at `knowledge/workflow-guide.md` for the full workflow-JSON rules.
- Destructive operations (publish, workflow/tag delete, execution stop) are gated by an explicit confirm-with-the-user-first rule in the guidance.

dsh-n8n-plugin README · ⚠️ Known limitations：- The n8n public API still has no cross-version stable "run workflow manually" endpoint; `n8n_webhook_call` fills that gap through the Webhook trigger — the workflow needs a Webhook node and must be published (or use `mode:"test"` while the editor listens for test events). Workflows without a Webhook trigger must be run in the n8n UI, then inspected with `n8n_executions` / `n8n_execution_get`.
- Public-API endpoints and fields differ across n8n versions (for example `publish/unpublish` alongside `activate/deactivate`, and builds that return no `versionId`). The plugin falls back on a 404 for publishing; `n8n_workflow_update` enforces optimistic concurrency whenever the instance exposes `versionId` (a stale base version is refused, never overwritten), reports `concurrency: "unsupported"` otherwise; other differences are reachable through `n8n_api`.
- Tags CRUD, workflow-tag read/write and execution stop rely on the instance exposing their public-API endpoints (`/tags`, `/workflows/{id}/tags`, `/executions/{id}/stop`). Older n8n builds return 404 there; upgrade the instance or use `n8n_api` for whatever it does expose.
- n8n caps tag names
